## What “Paused” means for a Supabase project When a Supabase project is in the **paused** state it simply means that the underlying cloud resources (database, storage, authentication service, Edge functions, etc.) are temporarily stopped to conserve resources. It’s **not** the same as deleting or deleting data. Your data **remains intact** – it’s just stored on disk, not actively running. --- ## Why projects get paused - **Free plan “idle” timeout** – if no traffic hits the project for a period (typically 30 days) Supabase will pause it to save on compute/DB costs. - **Billing status** – if your account were turned off or missing a payment method. - **Manual pause** – you or someone with permissions could have paused it yourself. On the Supabase dashboard you’ll see a banner: ``` ⚠️ Your project is paused – resume soon or risk termination ``` This is just a polite reminder of the policy. --- ## What happens to your data when paused | Resource | State when paused | What you can do | |----------|-------------------|-----------------| | PostgreSQL DB | Connection closed, accessible via `psql` or client tools if you use the raw connection string (you may need to `psql -h -U `) | You can still query the database from external clients or via the Supabase REST/GraphQL endpoints if they remain reachable, but the server isn’t actively listening for scheduled jobs etc. | | Supabase Auth | Stored in the DB; same as above | You can still list users offline via the REST API as soon as the project resumes | | Storage buckets | Data is stored on object storage (S3-compatible). | File objects stay in place; you can retrieve them once the project is resumed. | | Edge Functions | Deployed functions remain stored; you can rebuild or redeploy after resume. | > **Bottom line:** No data is wiped. Only the live, compute‐enabled aspect is turned off. --- ## How to resume your project | Platform | Steps | |---------|-------| | **Supabase web dashboard** | 1. Go to **Projects** in the sidebar.
2. Click on the paused project.
3. Press the “Resume Project” button (top right). | | **Supabase CLI** | Run `supabase stop` (to pause) and `supabase start` (to resume) if you have the CLI configured. | | **API (if needed)** | POST to `/rest/v1/projects/:id/resume` – usually not needed unless automating. | Once resumed it will re‑initiate the database, storage, auth, and any scheduled jobs. --- ## Things to keep in mind after resuming 1. **Database connection strings** – Make sure you update any local env files or editors if the host or credentials changed (rare, but possible after a long pause). 2. **Health checks** – Run a quick test: ```bash supabase db dump | grep "DROP" # just to confirm DB is responsive curl https://.supabase.co/auth/v1/users ``` 3. **Billing** – If you paused due to a billing issue, ensure your account is in good standing to avoid future pauses. --- ## FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | **Will my paid plan billing recur after pause?** | No. The free plan doesn’t bill, so nothing is charged while paused. | | **What if I pause and forget to resume?** | Supabase may automatically resume the next time any request hits the project. | | **Do I lose scheduled jobs?** | The SQL `cron` jobs remain stored; you might need to restart them. | | **Can I view logs during pause?** | Logs are frozen; you only see logs up to the pause moment. | --- ### Quick Checklist - **Resume the project** from the dashboard. - **Verify** connection via: ```bash supabase login supabase link --project-ref supabase db tsgen # just to trigger a DB reconnect ``` - **Test** a simple query or file upload to ensure everything works. --- **Bottom line:** Your data is safe. Pause is like putting the fridge on standby; the foods (database rows, files, users) stay there, just not actively cooling. Just hit *Resume* when you’re ready, and everything will be back online in seconds. If you have any more questions—about restoring old backups or about how long a pause can last—feel free to ask!
